He was ably supported by George Williams 2nd, Ray Hall 6th and Terry Clark(still a junior) 8th. The fine walking of John Knifton in his first 10 mile race was encouraging.
From our point of view this meeting was marred by an unpredictable judging decision given against George Williams when he was laying a comfortable second.
Eric Hall gave one of his usually polished performances to finish third, and he was followed by George Williams who walked in excellent style.

It was also notable for the performance of George Williams who came in at the last minute to replace Eric Hall, who had leg trouble. To finish fifth in such a class field at his first attempt over the distance deserves great praise.
In the two miles walk Belgrave swept to victory by filling the first three places; George Williams winning from Ray Middleton with John Knifton a good third in his first year of senior competition.
The winner of the match held in conjunction, was George Williams, who, walking very strongly was almost 30 seconds ahead of Eric. and Stan Vickers.

…Vickers (to finish second), Eric Hall (third, short of training and racing- but what pugnacity over the last mile!) and George Williams (how easy it all is!, fourth), gave us an impressive start, and with Ray Middleton not far away in 12th position team honours were won with only one other club havi…
With George Williams being passed by Clark(Poly) at 5 miles, when lying in 3rd place, and Ray Middleton walking home in 12th position, we had the low team score of 18 points.
Up Parkside, at the half distance, Eric had made up a 20 yard deficit on George Williams and Stan Vickers, and from then on was never again headed.

Our winning team was Ray Hall 2nd, John Knifton 3rd, George Williams 4th, Ray Middleton 6th. The Middlesex County Championship was held from Parliament Hill Fields and some of our members, walking as Cadogan A.C. showed up prominently but could be no match for the Metropolitan W.C. team.

George Williams persued a very even way in excellent style. Ray Middleton, our fourth man also once again demonstrated splendid style and ease of movement; and with a little more strength and experience- which could come very quickly- there is no doubt he will trouble them all.

George Williams had already notched up our first title the previous evening, outclassing the opposition to win in 14-51.2. The field was somewhat depleted here owing to the abstention of several walkers who did not approve of the walk being moved from the main day's events.
George Williams led from start to finish and Bobby Barnes gained his first Championship medal. Bert East took yet another handicap prize, with Harry Shields close behind.
George Williams fought out the lead with Misson (Met WC) for 12 miles, at which stage the pace proved too much for George and he faded to sixth place.

In a match versus the Stock Exchange, Stan, walking for the Exchange, improved his personal best time of the previous Saturday by four seconds with 13:26:4; over a minute ahead of George Williams.
Despite being without Stan Vickers, Eric Hall and George Williams---all taking a well earned rest---Belgrave still managed to notch up another victory in this premier event.

Although six of our leading runners were at Chelmsford the 36 starters were quite capable of producing an exciting race, especially as George Williams, one of our noted walkers, had chosen this race to return to the runners' fold.

The "easing off" of Eric Hall, the temporary retirement of Stan Vickers and the absence of George Williams seemed to give our rival clubs a moral uplift and a feeling that they were no longer fighting for second place.

Bobby Barnes, carrying the Middlesex colours for the first time, was our third scoring man and walked steadily throughout. George Williams completed the quartette, and despite being short of training walked a gallant race.

As we go to press we must congratulate Ray Middleton and George Williams on their being selected to represent Great Britain in the first round of the Europa Cup Walking Competition to be held at Wimbledon Park in conjunction with the Great Britain v Switzerland match on August 12th.
Ray Middleton and George Williams have filled these two gaps admirably, gained international colours, and formed the mainstay of several championship teams.

George Williams walked the 20 kilos to gain his second international vest and Ray Middleton made his debut for Great Britain in the 50. In the morning Ken Matthews led from start to finish to win the 20 by over 3 minutes in most convincing fashion.
Although Ken lost some ground nearing home he still won by some 400 metres and George Williams exceeded all hopes by beating some really hot opposition for third.
George Williams started well and led the field of 220 at the top of West Hill.

He stormed home by almost three minutes from our own George Williams who yet again mastered Bob Clark of the Poly. After two miles Matthews led by 100 yds from Williams, then came Clark a similar distance behind and some 80 yds back Ray Middleton was leading another group.
In the earlier stages, it did seem that George Williams might well gain second place but he was passed, first by Arthur Thomson and later by Bob Clark.

Belgrave were without George Williams and Ray Middleton and were consequently out of the championship picture. In the circumstances Ray Hall John Knifton, Bob Barnes and Ken Bailey put up sterling performances and we were not disgraced by our final fifth position.
Ray Middleton finished first in 54.19 from Nihill (Surrey) and our own Ray Hall and George Williams. The Bels won the team competition from Surrey and M.P.A.A.

After a brisk start it looked like a battle between Ray Middleton and George Williams for the individual championship, but from just before half-way, Ray opened up a 16 sec. lead and continued to increase this to 1 min. 17 secs. at the finish to annex this Trophy for the first time.
Will Belderson was awarded the Sir J.Coleman Cup. Unfortunately, George Williams was affected by the cold, never appeared to settle down and was disqualified in the first mile.
George Williams took the lead at 2 miles in 14:47 and was leading Clark by 11 secs. at 3 miles. In the next mile, however, Clark cut down this lead and was 1 sec. ahead of the Belgravian at 6 miles.

Only 200 yards from the finish George Williams was in 5th position and we were virtually assured of carrying off the team Championship.Unfortunately the effort was telling on George and during a bout of sickness, he was disqualified, and this decision apart from ruining our chances of first team pla…

George Williams who had travelled from Bournemouth was unwise to start after being laid low in bed with 'flu. He tried to set a fast pace and after leading Clark for 4 miles decided to retire owing to extreme cold.

George Williams began the season in terrific form with several fast 2 mile times and looked a strong candidate for the European Games, but George had the misfortune to be 'pulled' on a couple of occasions and was considerably disheartened as a result.
In the Surrey County Track Championships at Motspur Park, George Williams won the 2 mile title in a new County record of 14:05.4.
In the Inter-Counties meeting at the White City in June, George Williams (13:57.2) was 3rd in the 2 miles event and Ray Middleton 4th in the '7'.
On June 16th we travelled to Vauxhall Motors, Luton, for the open '20' and despite losing George Williams on the first lap we managed to bring home 10 of the 15 awards!
The absence of George Williams and Ray Middleton ( 2nd and 5th last year) and the loss of John Knifton during the race was too great a burden to bear in our effort to retain the Highgate title.

The 2nd leg was taken by George Williams better known in top class walking circles. This was George's first competitive relay run and performing like a veteran, he took us up one place and brought us 6 secs. nearer the leaders (Walton).
Next came George Williams the International Walker who only a few months ago was making a great name for himself by helping Great Britain to a win in the Europa Trophy.

George Williams who seems to have renounced walking for good, was showing good form and sound pace judgment only to be forced to drop back temporarily thro' an attack of catarrh soon after passing the church.

New faces are always welcome and this season the road running ranks have been swelled by Gerry North, Bill Kerr, Charlie Walker, George Williams John Moore and Peter Wrench; and with Jack Brown showing a return to form, things look good for next season.

In the absence of Barry Sawyer, Ken Miller, Clive Shippen, Laurie O'Hara, Derek Crookes and George Williams from the A team our hopes of a place as in the 1961 race were reduced to nil and the best we could do was to take 12th position out of the 69 teams that finished.
Dave King who looks more like George Williams in style every time he comes up from Bournemouth, finished 3rd in section 'B' covering 7miles 604yards.
